headline: MP MATERIALS Q3 EPS MISSES BY $0.06 — $0.10 Reported vs $0.16 Consensus; REE Producer Falls Short Day Before China Controls Expire
snippet: MP Materials (NYSE: MP), North America's only integrated rare earth miner, reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $0.10 against a $0.16 analyst consensus — a 37.5% miss. The result lands one day before China's year-long suspension of its October 2025 rare earth export controls expires on November 10, amplifying investor scrutiny of whether MP can ramp its own magnet manufacturing fast enough to matter if Beijing restores restrictions.

headline: CHINA'S 1-YEAR RARE EARTH TRUCE LAPSES NOVEMBER 10 — No Renewal Signaled; Sector Braces for 3 Possible Outcomes
snippet: China's one-year suspension of its expanded October 2025 rare earth export controls expires November 10, 2026, and Beijing has signaled no automatic renewal. Analysts outline three paths: a full extension, selective reimposition targeting specific elements or end-uses, or a full return to October 2025 restriction levels. With China still controlling an estimated 60-plus percent of global separation and refining capacity, the five-day countdown is the most consequential supply-chain event for heavy rare earth miners since the 2010–2012 quota crisis.

headline: EAGLE NUCLEAR (NUCL) BIDS ON NOBLE PLAINS URANIUM — Adds Powder River Basin and Shirley Basin ISR to Oregon Footprint
snippet: Eagle Nuclear Energy (Nasdaq: NUCL) signed a binding letter of intent to acquire 100% of Noble Plains Uranium in an all-stock deal, with Noble Plains shareholders receiving approximately 4.78% of Eagle's post-close equity at a deemed price of CAD $0.125 per share. The deal adds two Wyoming ISR projects — Duck Creek in the Powder River Basin (80% option held) and Shirley Central in the Shirley Basin — expanding Eagle beyond its flagship Aurora uranium project in Oregon into a second proven U.S. in-situ recovery jurisdiction.

headline: A$12.6B ASX GOLD MERGER — Genesis-Vault Scheme Creates Dominant Australian Mid-Tier; Implementation Due Late November
snippet: Genesis Minerals and Vault Minerals (ASX: VAU) are advancing a scheme of arrangement combining the two companies at an implied A$12.6 billion valuation for Vault, with shareholders to receive 0.7629 Genesis shares plus A$0.475 in cash per share. Implementation is targeted for late November 2026, in what analysts are calling the most significant Australian gold consolidation since the Newcrest-Newmont merger — and a signal that mid-tier M&A has resumed in earnest as gold holds above A$6,000 per ounce.

headline: INDIA APPROVES $297M LITHIUM AND NICKEL PROCESSING INCENTIVE — New Supply Chain Play vs Citi's Demand-Cut Pessimism
snippet: India approved a $297 million production-linked incentive programme targeting domestic lithium and nickel ore processing into high-purity compounds, aiming to reduce dependence on Chinese refining capacity. The announcement arrives less than a week after Citigroup cut its two-year lithium price forecast by 40%, signalling that government demand-side policy is now competing directly with market-driven supply pessimism to set the direction for critical mineral investment in emerging economies.

headline: STANDARD LITHIUM TARGETS YEAR-END GO/NO-GO — $1.45B SWA Direct Extraction Decision Narrows to Weeks
snippet: Standard Lithium (NYSE American: SLI) is targeting a final investment decision on its South West Arkansas direct lithium extraction project — with a capital cost estimate of approximately $1.45 billion — before year-end 2026. A go-ahead would make SWA one of the first commercial-scale DLE operations in North America and validate the technology stack at a moment when the broader lithium equity sector is trading near multi-year lows following Citigroup's demand-forecast downgrade.

headline: COPPERCORP LANDS TASMANIA GOVT DRILL GRANT — Final Jukes Assays Return 12m @ 0.54% Cu from 92m Depth
snippet: CopperCorp Resources (TSXV: CPER) released final core assays from hole JDD008 at the Jukes copper prospect in Tasmania, returning 12.0 metres at 0.54% copper, 0.14 g/t gold, and 0.89 g/t silver from 92 metres downhole, confirming sulphide-hosted copper at economic depths. The company simultaneously announced a Tasmanian government co-funded drilling grant, reducing future program costs and validating the geological prospectivity of one of Australia's least-explored copper terrains.

headline: CHINA GRABS TIBET COPPER-LITHIUM RIGHTS — Xizang Gaozheng Secures Mamupu Deposit; Shares SURGE on State-Backed Push
snippet: Xizang Gaozheng Civil Explosives, Tibet's dominant industrial explosives provider, secured mining rights for the Mamupu copper and lithium deposit in Tibet, sending shares sharply higher. The acquisition is part of a broader Beijing push to expand China's domestic resource base in copper and lithium as Western supply-chain diversification pressures intensify — mirroring China's simultaneous expansion of overseas mining stakes reported by multiple outlets on November 4.

headline: RARE EARTH AMERICAS: 29% HEAVY REE AT BRAZIL CLAY — Leach Recovery Boost Opens DLE Economics Path at Alpha Project
snippet: Rare Earth Americas (NYSE American: REA) reported that test samples from its Alpha clay project in Bahia, Brazil, showed heavy rare earth elements at approximately 29% of total REE content, excluding cerium — a significantly higher HREE proportion than typical ionic clay deposits and a key indicator for magnet-material economics. An improved leach recovery rate confirmed technical viability of a potential heap-leach-style extraction approach, putting Alpha on the short list of western hemisphere projects with the right grade basket for direct lithium extraction-style development.

headline: CAMECO FILES McARTHUR RIVER TECHNICAL REPORT — Sept 2026 Effective Date; World's Highest-Grade Uranium Mine Updated
snippet: Cameco (TSX: CCO) filed an updated NI 43-101 technical report on the McArthur River uranium operation in Saskatchewan, effective September 30, 2026, covering geology, mineral resources and reserves, mining methods, processing, environmental management, and an updated production plan. As the world's highest-grade uranium mine — averaging over 15% U₃O₈ — an up-to-date technical report strengthens Cameco's disclosure position ahead of upcoming licensing and capex review cycles as nuclear construction hits a 40-year high globally.

headline: USA RARE EARTH REPORTS NOV 9 — REE Scorecard Arrives One Day Before China's Nov 10 Export Control Decision
snippet: USA Rare Earth (Nasdaq: USAR) will report Q3 2026 results after market close on Monday, November 9, with a conference call scheduled for that afternoon — one trading day before China's October 2025 rare earth export control suspension expires on November 10. The timing convergence means USAR's earnings guidance on supply positioning and downstream contract pricing will carry unusual weight as the last major sector datapoint before Beijing announces its decision.

headline: KITCO OPINION: Gold & Silver Buyers in a Holding Pattern — 'One Thing' Could Break the Post-Midterm Stalemate
snippet: Kitco's November 3 opinion argues that gold and silver bulls remain in a holding pattern after the midterm-driven bounce, with investors waiting for a single confirmatory macro signal before committing new capital. The piece was published as gold sat near $3,900–$4,000 before the election results pushed it back above $4,000 — a rally that attracted momentum but, by this analysis, not yet the conviction needed to extend the move into a sustained new leg higher.
